context: A police officer briefs a uni reporter about logistics
purpose: Teach: 上回る/補給/含み/順次/終える/レギュラー/当店/常時

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 災害時の物資補給、レギュラーで訓練しています。
lines.en: We conduct disaster relief supply training on a regular schedule.
lines.style: Measured, official tone. Clear articulation on key terms. Steady pace, confident but not rehearsed. The cadence of someone trained to convey information precisely.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 当店レベルの店舗にも、順次配給があるんですか。
lines.en: Do smaller stores like ours get included in the distribution rotation?
lines.style: Genuine curiosity beneath the technical question. Lean forward slightly with 「順次配給」. Not rushed—careful to phrase it correctly. A hint of earnestness: he wants to understand the system, not just ask it.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: はい。常時想定を含み、訓練を終えるよう努めています。
lines.en: Yes. We make sure to complete our training accounting for every possible scenario.
lines.style: Formal but not cold. Slight pause after 「はい」 to signal importance. Measured delivery on procedural language. The warmth of someone who takes this seriously because it matters.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 訓練回数、年々上回るペースですか。
lines.en: Are the number of drills increasing year over year?
lines.style: Thoughtful follow-up. Soft landing on the question—no edge of interrogation. Natural conversational tempo. A genuine probe into whether preparedness is accelerating, not a challenge.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.style: Direct and factual. Slight emphasis on the affirmation. Brief—not sparse, but efficient. The answer of someone who respects the question enough not to pad it.
